channel.title: Los Angeles Review of Books – Reviews
channel.description: Book reviews from the Los Angeles Review of Books.

item.title: Murky Effects
item.description: A novel of desire and domestic disorder amid a disintegrating literary establishment.

item.title: The Impression of Living in a Ruin
item.description: Spanish author Elvira Navarro’s newly translated story collection captures the unease, decay, and isolation of our post-pandemic world.

item.title: Free Verse, Late Fame
item.description: Kent Jones’s film ‘Late Fame’ preaches the necessity of art while also decrying society’s escalating attempts to use it as a means of profit and power.

item.title: Snow Globe Palimpsest
item.description: Benjamin Moser delivers biographical sketches of Jews who refused to abandon the Diaspora.

item.title: A Humanism of Bad News
item.description: Revisiting Chekhov’s literary prescriptions for our divided times.

item.title: California Sons: Miriam Pawel’s “The Browns of California”
item.description: Jake Wertz reviews “The Browns of California,” a four-generation biography of the Brown family and a portrait of the state they shaped.

item.title: A Discount Heaven
item.description: Amy Fusselman’s new novel is an afterlife comedy about the importance of giving care.

item.title: Decolonizing the Dead
item.description: China Miéville’s first solo novel in over a decade is part Lovecraft, part le Carré—and quintessentially weird.

item.title: A Life Without a Paper Trail
item.description: Katie Bennett’s hybrid memoir intertwines her artistic coming-of-age with the story of Joan Vollmer and her murder by Beat author William Burroughs.

item.title: Generous Opacities
item.description: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha’s wide-ranging art practice is on display in a traveling retrospective.

item.title: A Slowed-Down Kind of Loving
item.description: Carol Armstrong explores how we write about still life.

item.title: Between Potatoes and Barley
item.description: An uncertain political pamphlet for uncertain times.

item.title: Lord Knows What I Am
item.description: What we can learn from the published correspondence of literary critic and academic titan Harold Bloom.

item.title: I Am Not the Same as Another Mother
item.description: Dorothea Lasky’s new poetry collection explores ‘elemental motherhood’ in all its horror and transformativity.
